speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: People understand, generally, that SBF flat prices are generally higher than BTO prices.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: But there are cases where SBF prices were lower, for instance, for the Punggol estate's Matilda Edge project.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Some units were quite significantly lower in prices during the SBF exercise in 2016, compared to the BTO prices in 2013.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Certain units at the lower floors were actually lower in price.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: So, the question now is: under what circumstances and considerations does HDB lower the price and, by doing so, is it fair to those who had bought the BTO flats in the same cluster?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I had mentioned, pricing can differ due to various reasons − a higher floor unit will be more expensive than a lower floor unit, and there are different characteristics of location as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, let us take all of that aside.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If the market has come down, then we charge it at a slightly lower price.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have been doing it all this while.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: BTO batch by BTO batch, sometimes the prices differ because of market conditions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Balance flats, as the market adjusts, we also update the pricing.
